t.7.59.1: Then, when night had set in, Śatrughna asked the brahmin Cyavana, the delight of the Bhṛgus, about the strength and weakness of Lavaṇa.
t.7.59.2: And what is the might of the trident, O brahmin? And who, having come to single combat, were formerly struck down by this point of the trident?
t.7.59.3: Having heard those words of the great-souled Śatrughna, the greatly radiant Cyavana replied to the delight of the Raghus.
t.7.59.5: Long ago in Ayodhyā there was a mighty king, the son of Yuvanāśva, renowned in the three worlds as Māndhātā, a man of great valour.
t.7.59.4: Countless are the deeds of this one, O bull among men; hear from me what befell him who was born in the Ikṣvāku lineage.
t.7.59.6: That lord of the earth, having brought the whole earth under his rule, then, as king, made preparations to conquer the world of the gods.
t.7.59.7: When Māndhātṛ had made his preparations out of a desire to conquer the world of the gods, intense fear arose in Indra and in the great-souled gods.
t.7.59.9: Knowing his wicked intention, Pākaśāsana spoke these words, beginning with conciliation, to the son of Yuvanāśva.
t.7.59.8: Honoured with half of Śakra's seat and half of his kingdom, and revered by the hosts of the gods, the king took a solemn vow.
t.7.59.10: You are a king in the world of men, O bull among men; without first bringing the earth under your sway, you seek here the kingship of the gods.
t.7.59.12: To Indra, who was speaking thus, Māndhātā spoke these words: "Where on the face of the earth, O Śakra, has my command been resisted?"
t.7.59.11: O hero, if the entire earth, in its wholeness, is under your control, then exercise the sovereignty of the gods here, together with your servants, army and mounts.
t.7.59.14: Hearing that dreadful and unwelcome speech uttered by the Thousand-eyed One, the king, ashamed and with his face cast down, was unable to say a word.
t.7.59.13: Sahasrākṣa said to him: "A rākṣasa named Lavaṇa, the son of Madhu, dwelling in Madhuvana, does not obey your command, O sinless one."
t.7.59.15: Having taken leave of the thousand-eyed one, the glorious lord of men, his face somewhat downcast with shame, came back once more to this world.
t.7.59.16: Harboring wrath in his heart, that blameless one, together with his servants, army and mounts, came to bring the son of Madhu under his control.
t.7.59.17: That bull among men, desiring Lavaṇa for battle, sent a messenger into the presence of Lavaṇa.
t.7.59.18: Having gone there, he spoke many unpleasant words to the son of Madhu; and as that messenger was speaking thus, the Rākṣasa devoured him.
t.7.59.19: But as the messenger delayed, the king, filled with anger, tormented that Rākṣasa on every side with a shower of arrows.
t.7.59.21: That blazing trident, having reduced the king to ashes along with his servants, army and mounts, returned once more to the hand of Lavaṇa.
t.7.59.20: Then Lavaṇa, laughing, seized the spear in his hand, and to slay his foe together with all his followers he hurled that supreme weapon.
t.7.59.22: Thus that very mighty king was slain together with his army and his mounts; and the power of the trident, O hero, is immeasurable and unsurpassed.
t.7.59.23: Tomorrow at daybreak you will slay Lavaṇa swiftly, while he has not yet taken up his weapon; of this there is no doubt, for your victory is certain.
